observations: All four 896x1152 native images and the exact four-view/390x844 phone consumer previews were inspected. The three-row sheet establishes transparent-edge appearance against light, gray and dark backgrounds.

The model now reads clearly as one compact upholstered mustard armchair with a broad puffy back, single sagged seat, two substantial arms and short brown feet. N/E/S/W form a consistent whole object without lingering sofa proportions.

Compared with draft-02, the back now has a broad asymmetric trough across its lit upper surface and a bowed lower front/recess. This gives visible worn padding under the fixed high source camera rather than a symmetric rectangular block.

The arm opening now exposes coherent brown slats behind thick irregular attached mustard folds and a ragged sleeve. In S the opening is plainly visible; E shows actual depth and folded cloth; N/W show plausible rear/side continuation. The thin outlined-box impression is materially improved.

The seat slit and three pale attached stuffing lobes remain readable in S/E, with a dark/folded lip leading into the pale cluster. The pale marking remains useful at phone size without becoming detached noise.

Broad warm highlights and ochre self shading describe rounded padding. No blown highlight, featureless black patch, ground shadow, clipping, distracting coplanar seam or material edge defect was visible in the required views.

At 390px phone width, all four chairs retain clear cushion/arm separation and single-chair identity among neighboring barrels. The S tear/tuft is still a useful contrast cue. The alpha-fitted gallery and clearance cards show matching undistorted native art.

Evidence-only packet corrects the style-reference metadata in the stable brief. Independent hash checks show the model, N/E/S/W, four-view-sheet and phone-consumer pixels are exactly the already inspected bytes. Frozen criteria and capture remain equal. The packaging blocker is resolved; no visual blocker remains.
remainingDifferences: The native source projection is higher than the ImageGen target, as required by the frozen contract. The front-back proportions are consequently seen from above rather than copied from the target camera.

Back sag is a broad asymmetric trough instead of the target's deeper central crescent. Torn fabric/wood construction is simpler and more faceted, while remaining coherent and soft within the current native family.
Stuffing uses three smooth chunky lobes rather than target fiber detail; small stains and rear repair are interpreted coherently rather than matching the single-view reference exactly.
